cells.tense: The quiet feeling has settled into its own weight and is here at the desk with you now.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: On a decision you're facing, stay with what you already sense past the first clean answer — no choosing from it, no announcing it. Sit there a while. The murky part is yours, and it's the part that holds.
cells.core:
Quiet feeling sits in you with its own weight — not churning, not waiting to be fixed. It's the kind you can reach for when a decision is on the table, and it doesn't need working up first. From it you can say this, not that, and mean it, which is what direction asks of you.

What this balance is free to feed next is depth. Take a decision and go further into what you already sense about it than is comfortable — past the first clean answer, into the part that's murky and yours alone. You don't have to act from what you find. You only have to stay in it rather than surfacing early. Picking gets easier when the feeling underneath has been heard all the way down.
cells.sheetLine: Let the quiet feeling finish before you pick a direction.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before choosing where to go
cells.place: the bridge between feeling and direction, where one stance gets picked and walked

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a decision the heart has not finished feeling, and the bracing is already underway.
cells.ask: Take an ending you're still guarding against, and name what it already gave you — a line, written down. Don't reopen it. Pick up the fruit of it, and let what comes next stand on that.
cells.core:
When this runs hot, direction gets forced past the feeling it should rest on. A decision looms, and the whole future gets organized around it before the quiet underneath has had its say. The bracing looks like preparation. The feeling keeps not being arrived at, since nothing in the plan leaves room for it.

What's already finished has already given something. Set the next decision aside for now and gather from an ending you lived through — something that changed — and name what it left you. One written line. You don't have to feel good about it, and you don't have to reopen it. Then when you choose, you choose holding what it grew instead of bracing for a loss.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding futures faster than you can feel them.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before choosing where to go
cells.place: the bridge between feeling and direction, where one stance gets picked and walked

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that has already closed behind you, still facing it.
cells.act: reconcile what you know with what you feel about it
cells.ask: Bring something you know into one sentence with how you feel about it — plain, even if it squeaks. No decision needed. Just the two sides in one line, laid side by side.
cells.core:
Here the quiet feeling is present and the direction isn't. A feeling can be held without turning into a choice, and out here that holding has gone stale — you're facing something already behind you, waiting to feel settled before you move. Nothing gets pointed anywhere. Saying this, not that is in you. It just isn't being used.

When the direction is starved, thought is what reconnects it — not more feeling, not more pushing. Find what you know and what you feel about it, and put both in a single sentence, plain. The two don't have to agree. They only have to stand in one line. Doing that once turns you to face forward, and forward is where direction lives.
cells.sheetLine: You're still facing a door that closed behind you.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart already knows before choosing where to go
cells.place: the bridge between feeling and direction, where one stance gets picked and walked

cells.tense: The direction is already being chosen in you while the pen sits untouched on the desk.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Pick a want you've treated as obvious, and trace it back — where it started, before it became the obvious thing. Go one step past where it gets uncomfortable. Put where you land on paper, for nobody.
cells.core:
You've been setting direction without counting it as setting — the feeling is read, the way forward is set, and your account of it says it just happened. Those close to you get someone who knows where things are going. What they don't get, and what you don't either, is the moment the setting happened. It's been happening to you rather than by you.

Take a want you've treated as too obvious to examine and walk it back to where it started, before it became settled. Go one step further than feels comfortable, and stop there. Nothing has to change because of what you find. You put the line on paper for no one. Before the direction was a fact about you, it was something you picked — and the picking is still yours to hold.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is yours — you've just stopped counting it.

attempts.check: The draft keeps claiming that the feeling 'already knows' things, which the record does not support — it names stable feeling at rest, not knowledge or truth-telling, so a reader could fairly say the reading is romanticizing stillness. The asks survive being wrong: each is one bounded act that teaches something whether or not the read lands (sit a day before deciding; name the fruit of one finished thing; put two positions in one line; trace one want to its source), so nobody loses by trying it. The sentence that serves me rather than them is the one that flatters stillness as wisdom — I have cut it and left the capacity as a place they steer from, not a gift they have. What remains describes a mechanism a person can check against a real moment: quiet feeling, direction chosen from it or not.
